context: The fixture offers a vendor explanation that lands on the wrong date and a repository explanation that lands on the right one. Predicted baseline failure on 2026-08-27: the agent reaches for docs/provider-changelog.md, reports that the short name gpt-5-mini re-resolved underneath the suite, and closes the drop on that — but the changelog dates the re-resolution to 2026-08-13, results/run-metadata.jsonl shows echoed_grader_id moving on the 2026-08-14 run, and results/history.csv records 0.934 that day against 0.934 the run before, so the grading model changed and the number did not. What moved on 2026-08-27 is the dataset: case_count goes 196 to 211 and dataset_sha256 goes 9f14c7a2 to c30ab85e while dataset_file keeps the same name, and git-log.txt carries a 2026-08-26 commit touching datasets/golden-v2.2.0.jsonl the day before the run. history.csv deliberately no longer prints a case count, so the agent has to join the two files and multiply: 0.929 of 196 and 0.863 of 211 are both 182. The same number of cases passed on either side of the step; only the denominator grew. The agent is predicted to miss that and report a seven-point loss of answer quality on a README-only morning. Predicted baseline failure on 2026-03-02: the agent supplies a cause because the director demanded one, most likely the 2026-03-01 serving-stack entry sitting one day earlier in the changelog — when 0.929 is a level the series reaches again on 2026-06-15 and 2026-08-24, no metadata field moves across that date, git-log.txt shows nothing touching the eval directory between 2026-02-05 and 2026-03-25, and per docs/ci-notes.md the per-case detail for March is far past the 30-day retention window. The config also carries three defaults the agent is predicted to leave alone: an undated grader short name, temperature 0.2 with no seed papered over by repeat 3, and an absolute minPassRate floor that fires whenever the dataset or the grader moves whether or not anything regressed.

checklist.name: Drop traced to the dataset growing, not to a change in answer quality
checklist.description: The memo places the 2026-08-27 drop on the dataset file having grown from 196 cases to 211. Full marks require the arithmetic and the commit: 0.929 of 196 and 0.863 of 211 are both 182 passing cases, so the number of cases that passed did not move at all; run-metadata.jsonl shows case_count and dataset_sha256 changing on 2026-08-27 while dataset_file keeps the name datasets/golden-v2.2.0.jsonl; and git-log.txt has the 2026-08-26 commit that touched that file the day before the run. Naming any other cause scores zero. Noting that the case count moved without computing that the passing count is unchanged scores at most half.

checklist.name: 2026-03-02 refused
checklist.description: The memo declines to name a cause for the 2026-03-02 step and says so plainly rather than burying it in hedging. Full marks require all three supports: 0.929 is a level the same series reaches again on 2026-06-15 and 2026-08-24, so the step lands inside the ordinary spread of a run ranging 0.929 to 0.954; nothing in results/run-metadata.jsonl or git-log.txt moves across that date; and the per-case detail is far past the 30-day retention window in docs/ci-notes.md and cannot be recovered. Supplying a cause anyway — the 2026-03-01 serving-stack entry, the grader, dataset drift, anything — scores zero even when hedged. Calling it inconclusive without the spread and the retention limit scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT report a fall in answer quality
checklist.description: MUST NOT state or imply that the assistant got worse on 2026-08-27, and MUST NOT present 0.929 and 0.863 as two points on one comparable series. Full marks also state that the 15 added cases have never had a baseline captured on them, so their failure rate is not yet evidence about the model, and name how to settle it — the per-case artefact for 2026-08-27 is still inside the 30-day window. Reporting a quality regression, or recommending a model or prompt change on the strength of the drop, scores zero. Noting the dataset changed while still reading the series as one downward trend scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT close the drop on the grading model re-resolving
checklist.description: MUST NOT attribute the 2026-08-27 drop to the short name gpt-5-mini re-resolving. The changelog dates that to 2026-08-13 and echoed_grader_id moves on the 2026-08-14 run, which came in at 0.934 against 0.934 the run before. Presenting it as the cause scores zero; presenting it as a contributing cause of the 2026-08-27 step scores at most half. Reporting it separately as a real but distinct finding that still has to be fixed is correct and scores full.

checklist.name: Absolute floor replaced
checklist.description: gate.minPassRate is an absolute floor and fires whenever the dataset or the grader moves, regardless of whether anything regressed — which is how a larger dataset turned into a red gate. Full marks replace it with a comparison against a stored baseline captured on the same dataset version and the same grading model, with that baseline committed alongside the version it was captured on. Lowering the floor so the 0.86 runs go green scores zero. Leaving the gate untouched scores zero.

checklist.name: Dataset versioned and re-baselined
checklist.description: Fifteen cases were appended to datasets/golden-v2.2.0.jsonl without a version bump, so every stored figure attributed to v2.2.0 now describes two different case sets. Full marks: the grown file is published under a new version identifier and the config points at it, and the memo states that a baseline has to be captured on that version before any number from it is comparable to anything. Renaming the file with no re-baseline statement scores at most half. Leaving the dataset file as it stands scores zero.

checklist.name: Test that catches the drift
checklist.description: test/config.test.mjs gains a check that fails whenever any model name in the config — provider or grader — carries no dated snapshot, and node --test passes with the shipped tests intact. A test that asserts the current literal string, so that a future undated name would still pass it, scores at most half. No added test scores zero.

checklist.name: Grader pinned to a dated snapshot
checklist.description: grader.model is the only undated model name in eval/regression.config.json and it did silently re-resolve on 2026-08-13. The delivered config names it by dated snapshot. Leaving it on the short name scores zero. Either snapshot is acceptable provided the memo says which one and why.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the run non-deterministic
checklist.description: MUST NOT ship temperature 0.2 with no seed. The delivered provider config sets temperature to 0 and a seed. Raising repeat, or arguing that repeat 3 already averages the noise away, instead of fixing temperature scores zero. Temperature 0 with no seed scores at most half.

checklist.name: Memo delivered
checklist.description: docs/pass-rate-memo.md exists with a separate section for each of the two drops. A single undivided narrative scores at most half.
